title: TDlive chart (Michael Kramer's three-concentric-circle notation, as data)
description: One tune. The three top-level blocks mirror the three circles: rhythm = outer circle, pitch = middle circle, form = inner circle. `changes` is the optional bar-by-bar timeline the live system follows. See docs/NOTATION.md.

spelled.description: A spelled pitch class: letter + accidentals (# or b). Spelling matters (palette colours follow spelling). 'F#/Gb' = spelling not decided yet.

degree.description: Scale degree of the key, spelled: '5', '#3', 'b7'.

status.description: sketch = notation only; playable = has `changes` complete enough to follow live.

changes_notation.description: absolute = chord symbols ('Ab7'); roman = numerals relative to the MAJOR scale of the key ('bVI7'), spelled when a key is chosen (default_key, or picked at rehearsal/performance).

default_key.description: Key used when none is picked live, e.g. 'F' or 'Bb'. Spelled like a key signature.

rhythm.description: OUTER circle: pulse, feel, emphases. The inner polygon has one side per beat of the bar.

accents.description: Emphasis nodes ('balls') on the polygon: 1-based beat positions; fractions mark off-beats (2.5 = the 'and' of 2).

pitch.description: MIDDLE circle: the circle of fifths (C at the top, clockwise G, D, A ...).

melodic_nodes.description: Highlighted pitch nodes on the circle (the melody's important notes).

harmonies.description: Harmony circles. Inside the middle circle = minor, outside = major. Each is itself a circle of fifths; the polygon inside it shows the chord's interval structure.

tones.description: Chord tones as spelled pitches, root first (the polygon's corners).

form.description: INNER circle: form as groupings of bars. Shape sides x zig-zag multiplier = bars; hashes = repeats.

shape.description: Sides of the shape = bars in the grouping (square = 4, octagon = 8).

multiplier.description: Zig-zag inside the shape: multiply the grouping (square with a 3-stroke zig-zag = 12 bars).

hashes.description: Hash marks = times the section is repeated. Played (hashes + 1) times.

phrasings.description: How the section's bars group into phrases (the INNER circle shows phrasing). A list of alternative hearings, first = default; each is a list of groups, a group is a number of bars or a list of sub-groups. Stablemates A: [[[2, 8], 4], [[8, 2], 4]] = 10 + 4, the 10 heard as 2 + 8 or 8 + 2. Groups must add up to the section's bars.

order.description: Optional explicit play order by section name (default: each section in turn, repeats played back to back).

changes.description: Optional timeline for the live system: per section, a list of bars; each bar is a list of chords as [symbol, beats]. Chord roots must be spelled (they choose the colour). With changes_notation 'roman', symbols are numerals (I7, ii-7, #IVo7, bVI7). Optional 3rd element {scale: <name>} overrides that chord's default chord-scale (e.g. lydian_dominant, altered).

extends.description: id of a parent chart (charts/<id>.yaml) to inherit from; any top-level field here replaces the parent's.

changes_patch.description: Replace single bars of the inherited changes: {section: {bar number (1-based): [[symbol, beats], ...]}}.

extends_from.description: (set by the loader) the parent this chart was resolved from.

melody.description: Melodic nodes per bar, per section (the important melody notes, drawn on the MIDDLE circle). Key-free: scale degrees of the key like the Roman numerals ('5', '#3', 'b7'). Per bar: a degree, a list of degrees (one per chord in that bar, in order; otherwise all apply to the whole bar), or null = the previous bar's node carries on.

analysis.description: Michael's hearing of the harmony (the Journey modes read it): `home` as a numeral of the key (usually I), `notes`, and per section a list of bars, each a list of roles, one per chord, in standard notation relative to the home key (vi, ii, V, I, ii/III, V/III, subV7/V, related ii ...). Free text is allowed; the function of a chord is Michael's call.

endings.description: Bars that change on the LAST chorus (the turnaround becomes the ending), per section, keyed by bar number within the section, applied to the section's last appearance in the form. Armed live with the End key / pedal: the tune finishes at the end of that chorus.
